title: edge_methods_data_access › Alternative data (tested 2026-11-19 from a non-Indian cloud IP)

body:
**What to automate (priority order)**
1. **Fetch + diff pipeline:** run `nse_fetch transcripts` → `pdftotext` → speaker-turn JSON with the management roster parsed from the cover page. This is fully scriptable now; the scratch code is `turns.py`.
2. **LLM extraction pass** with a fixed prompt that outputs the schema fields (quote, metric, target_low/high, unit, deadline, precision, volunteered flag, conditionality). A human then spot-checks about 20%. Expect about 8 candidates per call and a precision of about 70%.
3. **Auto-resolver for financial promises:** connect to screener quarterly and annual tables through `memdb metric`, so that revenue, OPM, FCF, capex and working-capital items score themselves once the quarter is reported. That is about 60% of the promises here.
4. **Restatement linker:** use embedding similarity on metric + deadline against open promises for the same ticker, then either attach to the existing promise (with status history) or create a new one. This also catches quiet target changes, for example a target number that differs from the last call while the wording says "maintain".
5. **"Stopped mentioning" detector:** track KPI terms per call (aftermarket %, Mexico USD, the 6.5m award, third platform 25–30%) and alert when a quantified KPI disappears for 2 or more calls.
6. **Candour tagger:** for each shortfall, check whether the next call's *opening remarks* mention it (unprompted) or whether it appears only in Q&A (prompted).
7. **Change-detector sidecar:** compare the management roster across calls (CFO, promoter attendance, IR host). This is cheap and flagged three changes here.

**Cost of this pilot:** about 100k words of transcript read, 68 promises, and roughly one person-day equivalent of work. With steps 1–4 automated, a quarterly update per company should take about 15 minutes of human review.

data.section: 7. Lessons learned on the method

title: UNIPARTS › 7. Lessons learned on the method

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:BAJFINANCE:fy27-aum-growth-26pct-plus`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.60 · **P(base)** 0.55 · resolve by 2027-05-15
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (19-Oct-2026): AUM +26.5% YoY to ₹5,84,624 cr; net AUM add ~₹38k cr/qtr for two quarters. CEO Rajeev Jain: 'probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis'; medium-term guide stays 20–25%. Headwinds named: RBI hikes ('baking in two more increases… 6% kind of rates'), NIM compression slightly worse than the 10–15 bps guide, gold-loan short-tenor schemes stopped, El Niño (monsoon 87% LPA). Track record: FY25 guide 26–27%, delivered ~26%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** BFL has a long record of hitting AUM guidance, and the guide was given with H1 already at 26.5%; but 26% is the bottom of the range and rate hikes plus rural stress lean against H2 acceleration. Slightly above base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A large lender restating a full-year growth range at H1 with H1 at/above the range bottom meets the range bottom roughly 55% of the time (range bottoms are often missed by tenths).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2027 ÷ consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2026 − 1 ≥ 26.0% (both as stated in BFL's Q4 FY27 results press release/investor deck; use BFL's own reported YoY if it states one).
- **Resolution source:** Bajaj Finance Q4 FY27 results press release / investor presentation (NSE announcements)
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/BAJFINANCE_23102026145254_BFL_Investor_Call_outcome_Transcript_for_filing.pdf

body:
Stage-2 test (106 case episodes, in-sample + 495-firm 2020 snapshot): current hard set caught 8/39 known traps,
rejected 0/62 winners — all 8 were frauds caught by *judgment* signals (fake cash, unverifiable profits, implausible
economics). Leverage blow-ups caught 0/15; post-run crashes 0/9. Auditor exit never fired before a peak (0/41) → it's
an EXIT trigger, not an entry screen. CFO/PAT<0.7 and negative FCF fired on winners as often as traps (HAL, BSE,
Trent, Netflix). Pledge >25% of promoter holding = best graded flag (8/20 traps vs 2/13 winners). P/E>50 belongs
in valuation. Universe test is survivorship-biased (no delisted firms) → can't see losers well.
**Adopted (provisional):** insight:disqualifiers-v2-proposal as the working rule set; solvency flags (negative
net worth, interest cover <1.5x, short-term funding of long assets, payouts > FCF while borrowing) are UNTESTED.

size-matched controls at 13 weeks (t −6.2) vs −2.08% live-only → bias small and in the predicted direction
(live-only understated the avoid leg). Long leg +1.00% net — not proven for the third time. Descriptive: distress-
listed firms after a bottom-two-quintile result lagged controls by −16.6% → combine the PEAD avoid flag with
pledge/solvency flags (stage 2 + 3 together). Status of the avoid leg: confirmed in 3 independent checks.
